heritage.story: After World War II, Ted Peters set up a smoker on Blind Pass Road in front of his Blue Anchor restaurant so passing drivers could see and smell the fish. By 1951 Ted Peters Famous Smoked Fish was running at its current location, with his half-brother Elry Lathrop as a partner. Tilla Lathrop created the German potato salad recipe still served today, and later generations of both families have run the business.

report:
# eat-pinellas: where to eat and drink in St. Pete, the Gulf beaches, Clearwater & North Pinellas, and day-trip towns

Checked 2026-09-27. 84 places (collection `places` only).

## What is covered

- **Historic and landmark restaurants**: Ted Peters Famous Smoked Fish (1951), The Chattaway, Harvey's 4th Street Grill (1984), El Cap, Skyway Jack's (1976), Bob Heilman's Beachcomber (1948), Crabby's Beachside Pavilion (the former Palm Pavilion), the Original Crabby Bill's (1983), The Hurricane (Pass-a-Grille, 1977), the Seahorse (Pass-a-Grille, 1938 building, rebuilt after Helene), Friendly Fisherman (John's Pass, 1978), Billy's Stone Crab (1972), O'Keefe's Tavern (1961), Bon Appétit (Dunedin, 1976), Casa Tina, Columbia Restaurant at Sand Key and at St. Armands Circle.
- **Frenchy's** (Clearwater Beach): Rockaway Grill and Saltwater Cafe. The Original Cafe and South Beach Cafe were left out (see below).
- **Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks Greek food**: Hellas Restaurant & Bakery (since 1970), Mykonos, Dimitri's on the Water, Mama's Greek Cuisine (1978), plus Rusty Bellies (seafood) and Tarpon Springs Distillery (ouzo, whiskey).
- **MICHELIN Guide Florida 2026** (announced May 28, 2026; first statewide guide). There are no starred restaurants in Pinellas, Sarasota or Polk. Recommended: Elliott Aster, Fortu, IL Ritorno, in between days and Sushi Sho Rexley (St. Pete); The Tides Market (Safety Harbor); Focaccia Sandwich + Bakery and Tralia (Sarasota); Nineteen61 (Lakeland). Bib Gourmand: Lucky 8 (Sarasota). Tags: michelin-recommended, michelin-bib-gourmand, michelin-2026. No Clearwater restaurant is in the 2026 selection.
- **Breweries and distilleries (18)**: Dunedin Brewery (its own claim, quoted and qualified: "the oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation" in Florida, brewing since 1996), 7venth Sun, Caledonia (Dunedin); 3 Daughters (St. Pete and Clearwater Beach), Green Bench (it says it was St. Pete's first microbrewery), St. Pete Brewing, Pinellas Ale Works, Cage, Gulfport Brewery, Mad Beach Brewing, Anecdote (Indian Rocks Beach), Grindhaus Brew Lab (Clearwater), Crooked Thumb (Safety Harbor), Rapp (Seminole), Brighter Days (Tarpon Springs); St. Petersburg Distillery and Tarpon Springs Distillery.
- **St. Pete Pier**: Teak, Pier Teaki (rooftop tiki bar), Doc Ford's, Fresco's.
- **Rooftop and cocktail bars**: The Canopy at The Birchwood, Pier Teaki, Hi-Fi Rooftop Bar (Fenway Hotel, Dunedin), Jimmy's Crow's Nest (Clearwater Beach), The Mandarin Hide, Gigglewaters (Safety Harbor, 1920s-themed bar with a classic-movie screen), COCKtail St. Pete (LGBTQ, Mari Jean Hotel).
- **Beach bars and waterfront**: Ka'Tiki (1982), Undertow, Mahuffer's, Shephard's Tiki Bar, Paradise Grille, Buoy's, O'Maddy's (Gulfport), Guppy's, Salt Rock Grill, Island Way Grill, Caretta on the Gulf, Maritana (Don CeSar).
- **Food hall**: Central Park St. Pete Food Hall (551 Central Ave, old Woolworth building; phased opening from Feb 2026).
- **Other St. Pete**: Bodega (Cuban sandwich), Parkshore Grill (Beach Drive since 1996), BellaBrava (2005).
- **Day trips**: Star Fish Company (Cortez, dates to the 1920s), Mar Vista (Longboat Key, c. 1912 building), Sandbar (Anna Maria, site history to 1911, bought 1979), Rod & Reel Pier (status below), Yoder's (Sarasota Amish cooking since 1975), Columbia St. Armands, and the four Michelin picks in Sarasota and Lakeland.

## Counts

- By kind: restaurant 54, brewery 16, bar 10, distillery-winery 2, cafe-bakery 1, food-hall 1.
- By region: St. Petersburg 29, Gulf Beaches 25, Clearwater & North Pinellas 20, Day Trips 10.
- By area: downtown-stpete 16, clearwater-beach 9, tarpon-springs 7, dunedin 7, grand-central 6, sarasota 5, indian-rocks-beach 5, bradenton-anna-maria 4, pass-a-grille 3, safety-harbor 3, st-pete-beach 3, south-stpete 2, old-northeast 2, gulfport 2, madeira-beach 2, downtown-clearwater 2, west-stpete 1, sand-key 1, polk 1, largo 1, fort-de-soto 1, treasure-island 1.
- Status: open 83, temporarily-closed 1 (Rod & Reel Pier). signature: true on 5 (Ted Peters, Frenchy's Rockaway Grill, The Hurricane, Hellas, Dunedin Brewery). Heritage blocks on 4 (Ted Peters, Star Fish Company, Mar Vista, Sandbar).
- Source: 73 records use the business's own page as source_url. 11 fall back to a Visit St. Pete-Clearwater profile or list because the business site blocked both fetchers or has no site (Frenchy's Rockaway, Billy's Stone Crab, Dimitri's, Fresco's, Mykonos, Mahuffer's, Undertow, El Cap, Brighter Days, Shephard's Tiki Bar, Casa Tina). Also: Visit Sarasota for Lucky 8, FOX 13 for the Seahorse and Rod & Reel, and I Love the Burg for Frenchy's Saltwater Cafe.

## How candidates were found

1. Visit St. Pete-Clearwater lists, read with WebFetch: the Eat & Drink dining hub, "Landmark Restaurants", "Best Waterfront Restaurants", "MICHELIN-Recognized Restaurants", the Gulp Coast Craft Beer Trail (north, central and south region pages), Drinks, Nightlife, "Best Rooftop Bars & Restaurants" and the LGBTQ travel page. The individual profiles were used for addresses, phones and hours where a business site blocked us.
2. The MICHELIN Guide 2026 Florida announcement on michelinmedia.com (read with curl; the full Bib Gourmand, starred and recommended tables are images on that page and were read one by one). guide.michelin.com returned empty pages to both fetchers.
3. Visit Sarasota's Michelin article, WWSB/mysuncoast (Tralia and the first Sarasota Michelin picks) and the Columbia Restaurant locations page.
4. The St. Pete Pier restaurants page (stpetepier.org/restaurants) and the SpongeDocks.net Tarpon Springs restaurant list.
5. News checks for storm damage and closures: FOX 13 (Seahorse reopening, Rod & Reel moving on land, Central Park food hall), I Love the Burg (Frenchy's reopenings, Nov 2024) and Axios (Cycle Brewing taproom closing).
6. Search: the session's WebSearch budget was already used up, and Bing/DuckDuckGo/Google HTML pages were blocked or broken, so discovery used Marginalia Search (via curl) plus direct fetches of known official sites.
7. Quotes: every quote was checked against page text read with curl, or taken from a page read directly. Quotes that reached me only through WebFetch's summarizer (mostly Visit St. Pete-Clearwater profiles, and Visit Sarasota for Lucky 8) were dropped, because two reads of the same page returned different wording. 68 records have a quote.

## Deliberately left out (and why)

- **Cycle Brewing** (St. Pete): Axios (May 6, 2025) reported the downtown taproom closing. The article itself was blocked, and cyclebrewing.com shows "This store is unavailable". Current status is not confirmed.
- **Frenchy's Original Cafe and Frenchy's South Beach Cafe**: frenchysonline.com blocks both fetchers, and no readable page gives their current addresses. I Love the Burg (Nov 2024) says the original cafe had reopened.
- **Woody's Waterfront** (St. Pete Beach): the site's domain did not resolve, and there was no tourism profile.
- **Coney Island Grill** (St. Pete, hot dogs): coneyislandgrill.com is now an unrelated template site, and the status could not be confirmed. **Munch's** had no site found.
- **Flanagan's Irish Pub** (Dunedin): its domain is for sale, and the status is unconfirmed.
- **Merry Pier** (Pass-a-Grille bait shop and pier) is left to the outdoors/see slices, and its status is unknown. The **Anna Maria City Pier** restaurant and **Beach House** (Bradenton Beach) are not covered.
- **Chains and hotel lobby bars** without a local story; **Kahwa Coffee** (a St. Pete-founded chain with no single flagship identified); Crabby Bill's St. Pete Beach and Palm Harbor branches (mentioned in the main record); smaller Gulp Coast breweries (Bayboro, Overflow, Grand Central Brewhouse, Cueni, HOB, Woodwright, Soggy Bottom, Stilt House, de Bine, Two Frogs, Unrefined, Arkane, Southern Lights, Sea Dog, Mastry's Brewing, Troubled Waters).
- **Palm Harbor and Oldsmar** have no records; nothing there met the brief's "historic or signature" bar in the lists read.
- **Sarasota** is limited to Michelin picks, the Columbia and Yoder's (historic), as the brief asked.

## Open questions for the verifier

1. **Seahorse Restaurant (Pass-a-Grille)**: FOX 13 (Jan 26, 2026) said it would reopen the next week. Confirm it is serving and add its street address. The record has no address or coordinates.
2. **Rod & Reel Pier**: the pier was washed away by Milton. Is the Holmes Beach replacement (former Old Hamburg Schnitzelhaus) open, and at what address? Is the pier being rebuilt?
3. **Status from tourism profiles only** (no official site readable): Frenchy's Rockaway Grill (reported still recovering in Nov 2024; profile now lists hours), Mykonos (Facebook page only), Mahuffer's, Undertow, Billy's Stone Crab, Dimitri's, El Cap.
4. **Hours left unknown because sources disagree**: in between days, Tralia, Tarpon Springs Distillery, Mama's Greek Cuisine, Star Fish Company.
5. **Area judgment calls**: Ted Peters is in the city of South Pasadena (filed under west-stpete); Harvey's and El Cap (4th St N at 31st–35th Ave) are filed under old-northeast.
6. **Own claims, quoted and attributed only**: Dunedin Brewery ("oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation"), Green Bench ("St. Petersburg's first microbrewery"), Crabby's Beachside Pavilion ("oldest beach pavilion in Florida"), Columbia St. Armands ("oldest operating restaurant in Sarasota"), Caretta on the Gulf ("Clearwater's only AAA Four-Diamond" restaurant), Parkshore Grill ("first major restaurant" on Beach Drive), Anecdote ("closest brewery to the Gulf beach").
7. **The Chattaway**: Visit St. Pete-Clearwater says it opened in 1951; the restaurant says "over 90 years" in one form or another.

## Verification (2026-09-27)

An adversarial re-read of every record by a second agent. Result: 84 records checked, 33 corrected, 0 removed, 6 added (90 places now: restaurant 58, brewery 16, bar 11, distillery-winery 3, cafe-bakery 1, food-hall 1; St. Petersburg 30, Gulf Beaches 29, Clearwater & North Pinellas 20, Day Trips 11; open 89, temporarily-closed 1). Validator: 0 errors.

**How.** Every source_url, also_source, url and quote_source was fetched again with curl (browser user agent) and the page text searched for each record's address, phone, hours, years, names and quote; pages that block curl (Visit St. Pete-Clearwater profiles, frenchysonline.com, dimitrisonthewater.com, the Columbia and Tarpon Springs Distillery hour tables, cocktailstpete.com) were read with WebFetch. Every quote was re-matched verbatim against curl text (COCKtail's short quote only through WebFetch). The MICHELIN 2026 Florida lists were re-read from the press page's image tables (Recco_1_3 … Recco_6_2, BG1–2, Star_2_2): the nine recommended and one Bib Gourmand picks in the slice are all there, and there are no starred restaurants and no other Pinellas, Sarasota or Polk entries. Every address was re-geocoded (Census); all points are within 60 m except Teak/Pier Teaki (OpenStreetMap point at the pier head, correct) and Ka'Tiki (OpenStreetMap point on West Gulf Blvd, correct). Closures were checked with Google News RSS searches (WebSearch was unavailable; the RSS links were resolved to publisher URLs) plus Creative Loafing's Jun 19, 2026 roundup of reopened Pinellas beach bars and I Love the Burg's May 18, 2026 guide to open beach bars.

**Status findings.** The Chattaway was about to close earlier in 2026 and reopened on Sep 25, 2026 under new owners (St Pete Rising). The Seahorse (Pass-a-Grille) reopened in early February 2026 at 800 Pass-a-Grille Way (address was missing). The Rod & Reel's landside restaurant opened Nov 21, 2025 at 3246 East Bay Dr, Holmes Beach; the pier itself stays temporarily-closed pending a rebuild. The Hurricane reopened by Oct 28, 2024 (FOX 13). Paradise Grille (Jan 2025), Mad Beach Brewing (Oct 2024), Undertow, Ka'Tiki, Shephard's, Frenchy's Rockaway, Crabby's Pavilion, Billy's Stone Crab, O'Maddy's (new rooftop, Jun 2026), Mahuffer's and Sandbar all have 2025–2026 evidence of operating. Not included, with reasons: The Dewey (Pass-a-Grille) never reopened after 2024 (St Pete Rising, Jun 30, 2026: its space is becoming Moon by Malio's); Cycle Brewing closed its downtown St. Pete taproom in May 2025 (St Pete Rising, Tampa Bay Times); Munch's closed in Dec 2022; Gators Cafe (John's Pass) closed in 2020.

**Corrected (33).** chattaway (new source, summary, dropped the old owners' tea price and quote); pier-teaki (hours; removed a 21+ claim that came from a guest review); columbia-restaurant-sand-key and -st-armands (phones; Our Story page added for the 1905 Ybor founding); frenchys-rockaway-grill and frenchys-saltwater-cafe (official pages now the source; hours, phone; Saltwater's quote was a news sentence and was dropped); in-between-days, focaccia-sandwich-bakery, st-petersburg-distillery, rusty-bellies-waterfront-grill, salt-rock-grill, gulfport-brewery-eatery, brighter-days-brewing, okeefes-tavern, billys-stone-crab, cocktail-st-pete (unsupported details removed from summaries: small plates, a chef's name, Pinellas Trail, tiki bar/live music, Intracoastal view, dogs, garage door, dish names, 'thousands of traps', '21 and up'); lucky-8 (official site now readable: source, phone, hours, verbatim quote); dimitris-on-the-water (official site: address is 690, not 698 Dodecanese; hours with Wednesday closed; family-owned since 2010; re-geocoded); hellas, tarpon-springs-distillery, skyway-jacks, caretta-on-the-gulf, buoys (hours from the official pages); crooked-thumb-brewery (quote and '20 taps' not on any page read: removed; hours added); 3-daughters-brewing (quote_source); green-bench-brewing (Upstairs at Webb's, opened Sep 25, 2026); island-way-grill, jimmys-crows-nest (summaries rewritten from the official sites); central-park-st-pete-food-hall (FOX 13 says it stands where the Woolworth building was, not in it); omaddys (street suffix S, official hours); bellabrava (hours dropped: two conflicting tables; third location noted); seahorse and rod-and-reel-pier (above). Every other record got a dated VERIFIER note saying what was re-read.

**Added (6).** frenchys-original-cafe (the 1981 original, 41 Baymont St) and frenchys-south-beach-cafe (351 S Gulfview Blvd), both from frenchysonline.com; rod-and-reel-holmes-beach (AMI Sun, Nov 25, 2025; Bay News 9); caddys-treasure-island (caddys.com, reopened April 2026 after an 18-month rebuild); wharf-pass-a-grille (wharfpag.com: open since 1994 in a building on 1912 pilings); florida-orange-groves-winery (floridawine.com, South Pasadena). Mazzaro's Italian Market was considered but see-pinellas already holds mazzaros-italian-market, so it is not duplicated here.

**Open questions for the merge.** Mykonos, Undertow, Mahuffer's, El Cap, Billy's, Fresco's, Casa Tina and Brighter Days still rest on tourism profiles (no readable official site). BellaBrava and in between days have no hours. Rod & Reel Holmes Beach hours are as of Nov 2025 (rodandreelpier.com did not respond). The Friendly Tavern (Redington Shores, 1947) and Dockside Dave's (Madeira Beach) both reopened in 2026 but had no readable official page, so they were left out.
